\section[el escenario]{el escenario — the stage; the setting}

\label{lesson:ES-C759-escenario}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to skate, then the Spanish for the fan.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el escenario}
\textbf{el escenario} — \textquotedblleft{}the stage; the setting\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El cantante salió al escenario.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The singer came out on stage.}
\end{quote}

Also a setting or scenario: \emph{el escenario del crimen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{escenario} is built on \emph{escena} with the ending \emph{-ario}; \emph{escena} comes from Latin \emph{scaena}, from Greek \emph{skēn\'{\={e}}} \textquotedblleft{}tent, stage\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el escenario}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el escenario}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el escenario}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to skate, then the Spanish for the fan, then say \emph{el escenario} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el escenario mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The stage; the setting\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el espectáculo]{el espectáculo — the show}

\label{lesson:ES-C759-espectaculo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the fan, then the Spanish for the stage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el espectáculo}
\textbf{el espectáculo} — \textquotedblleft{}the show\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El espectáculo empieza a las ocho.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The show starts at eight.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Dar un espectáculo} — to make a scene.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{espectáculo} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{spectāculum} \textquotedblleft{}sight, show\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{spectāre} \textquotedblleft{}to watch\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the fan, then the Spanish for the stage, then say \emph{el espectáculo} again

\section[aplaudir]{aplaudir — to applaud, to clap}

\label{lesson:ES-C759-aplaudir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the stage, then the Spanish for the show.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: aplaudir}
\textbf{aplaudir} — \textquotedblleft{}to applaud, to clap\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Al final, todos aplaudieron.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{At the end, everyone clapped.}
\end{quote}

\emph{El aplauso} — applause.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{aplaudir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{applaudere} \textquotedblleft{}to clap the hands together\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{plaudere} \textquotedblleft{}to strike, to clap\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[actuar]{actuar — to act, to perform}

\label{lesson:ES-C759-actuar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the show, then the Spanish for to applaud.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: actuar}
\textbf{actuar} — \textquotedblleft{}to act, to perform\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Actúa en una obra de teatro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She is acting in a play.}
\end{quote}

Also to act, to take action. Forms: \emph{actúo}, \emph{actúas}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{actuar} comes from Medieval Latin \emph{āctuāre} \textquotedblleft{}to put into action\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{āctus}, from \emph{agere} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{actuar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{actuar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the show, then the Spanish for to applaud, then say \emph{actuar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[la actuación]{la actuación — the performance}

\label{lesson:ES-C759-actuacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to applaud, then the Spanish for to act.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la actuación}
\textbf{la actuación} — \textquotedblleft{}the performance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Su actuación fue increíble.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{His performance was incredible.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{actuación} is built on \emph{actuar} with the ending \emph{-ción}; \emph{actuar} comes from Medieval Latin \emph{āctuāre} (EtymDB), from \emph{agere} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item the musician, to hum, the song, rhythm, to compose
  \item to knit, fishing, pottery, gardening, to sew
  \item the warm-up, to jog, the athlete, to get injured, the muscle
  \item the forward, to score, the scoreboard, the referee, to draw

  \item volleyball, boxing, to ski, to skate, the fan

Chess? (\textbf{el ajedrez}.) The jigsaw puzzle? (\textbf{el rompecabezas}.) The pack of cards? (\textbf{la baraja}.) Magic? (\textbf{la magia}.) To bet? (\textbf{apostar}.) The musician? (\textbf{el músico}.) To hum? (\textbf{tararear}.) The song? (\textbf{la canción}.) Rhythm? (\textbf{el ritmo}.) To compose? (\textbf{componer}.) To knit? (\textbf{tejer}.) Fishing? (\textbf{la pesca}.) Pottery? (\textbf{la cerámica}.) Gardening? (\textbf{la jardinería}.) To sew? (\textbf{coser}.) The warm-up? (\textbf{el calentamiento}.) To jog? (\textbf{trotar}.) The athlete? (\textbf{el atleta}.) To get injured? (\textbf{lesionarse}.) The muscle? (\textbf{el músculo}.) The forward? (\textbf{el delantero}.) To score? (\textbf{marcar}.) The scoreboard? (\textbf{el marcador}.) The referee? (\textbf{el árbitro}.) To draw? (\textbf{empatar}.) The champion? (\textbf{el campeón}.) The tournament? (\textbf{el torneo}.) Victory? (\textbf{la victoria}.) Defeat? (\textbf{la derrota}.) The medal? (\textbf{la medalla}.) Volleyball? (\textbf{el voleibol}.) Boxing? (\textbf{el boxeo}.) To ski? (\textbf{esquiar}.) To skate? (\textbf{patinar}.) The fan? (\textbf{el aficionado}.) The stage? (\textbf{el escenario}.) The show? (\textbf{el espectáculo}.) To applaud? (\textbf{aplaudir}.) To act? (\textbf{actuar}.) The performance? (\textbf{la actuación}.)
